stages.name: Other kingdoms
stages.desc: Egypt, Lydia, Media or free kings of Cyprus, outside the empires of Babylon and Persia

stages.name: Babylonian-held
stages.desc: Ruled by or tributary to Nebuchadnezzar's Neo-Babylonian empire

stages.name: Persian-held
stages.desc: Part of the Achaemenid Persian empire, as satrapy or vassal kingdom

stages.name: Independent Phoenician city
stages.desc: Phoenician city-states governing themselves, free of an imperial overlord

stages.name: Besieged
stages.desc: Under siege, or crushed after revolt, that year

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Independent Greek and Phoenician city-kingdoms such as Salamis, Kition and Paphos
Pharaoh Amasis makes the kings of Cyprus tributary to Egypt
The Cypriot kings go over to Persia and join Cambyses against Egypt
Cyprus joins the Ionian Revolt; the Persians besiege Soli for five months
The revolt is crushed and Persian rule restored
Evagoras of Salamis rebels and wins much of the island
The Persian fleet defeats Evagoras off Kition and besieges Salamis
Evagoras submits and keeps Salamis as a tributary king
The Cypriot kings bring 120 ships to Alexander at Sidon

states.name: Israel
timeline: Jerusalem is destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar's army and Judah becomes a Babylonian province
Under Persia; exiles are allowed to return to Judah
The coast submits to Alexander after the fall of Tyre; Gaza resists two months

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Babylonian troops encamp opposite island Tyre, ruled by King Ithobaal III
Tyre comes to terms after thirteen years, by Josephus's count, and accepts Babylonian overlordship
Tyre is governed by short-lived judges instead of kings, according to Josephus
The Tyrians fetch kings from Babylon: Merbaal, then Hiram III
Babylon falls to Cyrus; the Phoenician cities become Persian vassals
Tyre's fleet serves Cambyses in Egypt but refuses to sail against Carthage
Evagoras of Salamis briefly takes Tyre, c. 387 BC
Sidon leads the Phoenician cities in revolt against Artaxerxes III
Sidon is betrayed and burns; the revolt collapses
Persian rule is restored along the Phoenician coast
After Issus, Persian rule collapses; Sidon and Byblos open their gates to Alexander, Tyre declares itself neutral
Tyre falls in July after a seven-month siege and a causeway built across the strait

states.name: Syria
timeline: Babylonian province since Nebuchadnezzar's victory at Carchemish in 605 BC
Part of Persia's satrapy 'Beyond the River'
After Issus, Parmenion seizes Damascus and the Persian treasure

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Lydia in the west, Media in the east
Lydia and Media make peace on the Halys after an eclipse
Cyrus conquers Lydia and takes Sardis
Alexander crosses the Hellespont and wins at the Granicus

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Babylonia, heartland of Nebuchadnezzar II's empire
Nebuchadnezzar dies after forty-three years on the throne
Cyrus the Great enters Babylon

states.name: Jordan
timeline: The kingdoms of Ammon, Moab and Edom are tributaries of Babylon
Nebuchadnezzar campaigns against Ammon and Moab, according to Josephus
Under Persian rule
Persian authority east of the Jordan passes to Alexander

states.name: Egypt
timeline: The Saite pharaohs of Egypt, Babylon's great rival
Amasis overthrows Apries and takes the throne
Cambyses defeats Psamtik III at Pelusium and conquers Egypt
Egypt breaks free under Amyrtaeus
Artaxerxes III reconquers Egypt; Nectanebo II flees south
The Persian satrap surrenders Egypt to Alexander late in the year

events.title: Jerusalem destroyed
events.text: Nebuchadnezzar's army burns Jerusalem and its temple and deports much of Judah's population to Babylonia.

events.title: Riblah
events.text: From his headquarters at Riblah on the Orontes, Nebuchadnezzar directs his western wars; Judah's king Zedekiah is blinded there.

events.title: Ezekiel's oracle
events.text: Among the exiles in Babylonia, the prophet Ezekiel foretells that Tyre will become 'a place for spreading nets'.

events.title: Tyre besieged
events.text: Babylonian troops encamp on the mainland facing the island city of King Ithobaal III.

events.title: Battle of the Eclipse
events.text: Lydia and Media, at war on the Halys, make peace after a solar eclipse darkens the battlefield.

events.title: Ammon and Moab
events.text: Josephus records a Babylonian campaign east of the Jordan, five years after Jerusalem's fall.

events.title: Apries at sea
events.text: Herodotus says Pharaoh Apries sent an army against Sidon and fought the Tyrians at sea.

events.title: Tyre submits
events.text: After thirteen years, by Josephus's count, Tyre comes to terms without being stormed.

events.title: Amasis seizes power
events.text: The general Amasis overthrows Pharaoh Apries at Sais and rules Egypt for forty-four years.

events.title: Egypt takes Cyprus
events.text: Herodotus credits Amasis with making the kings of Cyprus pay him tribute.

events.title: Babylon strikes Egypt
events.text: A Babylonian chronicle fragment records Nebuchadnezzar marching against Amasis.

events.title: Judges in Tyre
events.text: Josephus lists judges, not kings, governing Tyre for several years.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar dies
events.text: The conqueror of Jerusalem and besieger of Tyre dies in Babylon.

events.title: Kings from Babylon
events.text: The Tyrians send to Babylon for princes held there: Merbaal, then his brother Hiram III.

events.title: Cyrus takes Media
events.text: Cyrus of Persia overthrows his Median overlord and seizes Ecbatana.

events.title: Sardis falls
events.text: Cyrus defeats Croesus of Lydia and takes his capital.

events.title: Babylon falls
events.text: Cyrus enters Babylon; its empire, Phoenicia included, passes to Persia.

events.title: Exiles return
events.text: Cyrus lets the Judean exiles go home; Tyre and Sidon supply cedar for the new temple.

events.title: Cyprus goes over
events.text: The kings of Cyprus abandon Egypt and join Persia, Herodotus reports.

events.title: Pelusium
events.text: Cambyses defeats Psamtik III and conquers Egypt, his fleet manned largely by Phoenicians.

events.title: No war on Carthage
events.text: The Phoenicians refuse to sail against Carthage, their own colony, and Cambyses gives way.

events.title: Beyond the River
events.text: Darius organises Syria, Phoenicia and Cyprus into a single tribute district.

events.title: Cyprus revolts
events.text: Onesilus of Salamis joins the Ionian Revolt; a Phoenician fleet ferries the Persian army to the island.

events.title: Soli besieged
events.text: The Persians undermine the walls of Soli and take it in the fifth month.

events.title: Battle of Lade
events.text: Phoenician squadrons lead the Persian fleet that crushes the Ionians off Miletus.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.text: Xerxes' fleet, its core Phoenician, is defeated by the Greeks in the straits of Salamis.

events.title: Salamis in Cyprus
events.text: An Athenian fleet defeats Phoenician and Cilician ships off Salamis in Cyprus.

events.title: Egypt breaks free
events.text: Amyrtaeus of Sais ends Persian rule; Egypt stays independent for sixty years.

events.title: Evagoras rebels
events.text: Evagoras, Greek king of Salamis, sets out to unite Cyprus against Persia.

events.title: Evagoras takes Tyre
events.text: With Egyptian help, Evagoras takes Tyre by storm, says Diodorus, c. 387 BC.

events.title: Battle of Kition
events.text: The Persian fleet defeats Evagoras at sea and besieges Salamis.

events.title: Sidon revolts
events.text: King Tennes of Sidon leads the Phoenician cities in revolt against Artaxerxes III.

events.title: Sidon burns
events.text: Betrayed by Tennes, the Sidonians set fire to their own city; Diodorus claims forty thousand died.

events.title: Egypt reconquered
events.text: Artaxerxes III takes Pelusium and ends Egypt's independence.

events.title: The Granicus
events.text: Alexander of Macedon defeats the Persian satraps of Anatolia.

events.title: Battle of Issus
events.text: Alexander routs Darius III in November; the road to Phoenicia lies open.

events.title: Damascus taken
events.text: Parmenion captures the Persian baggage train and treasury.

events.title: Phoenicia submits
events.text: Arwad, Byblos and Sidon open their gates; Alexander makes Abdalonymus king of Sidon.

events.title: Tyre refuses
events.text: The Tyrians refuse Alexander's request to sacrifice in Melqart's temple; in January the siege begins.

events.title: The causeway
events.text: The Macedonians build a mole about eight hundred metres long across the strait to the island.

events.title: Fleets change sides
events.text: The kings of Arwad, Byblos, Sidon and Cyprus bring over two hundred warships to Alexander.

events.title: Tyre stormed
events.text: After seven months, Macedonian troops breach the walls; thousands are killed and enslaved.

events.title: Siege of Gaza
events.text: Gaza holds out for two months before it, too, is stormed.

events.title: Egypt submits
events.text: The Persian satrap Mazaces surrenders Egypt to Alexander without a fight.

chartNote: Share of the area of eight present-day countries, by the power that held most of each. Regions are today's boundaries, standing in for ancient kingdoms, satrapies and city-states, and Lebanon stands for Tyre and the Phoenician coast. A simplification: the Phoenician cities kept their own kings under every empire, ancient dates are approximate, and the large countries (Turkey, Egypt) swing the shares.
